scenario.fault_family: access port in wrong VLAN (misdirected prompt)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8044: PC5 in Campus 1 lost its default gateway (172.16.10.254) while
PC6/PC7/PC8 on the same access switch are fine. PC5 still has link. The team
thinks switch4 -- the upstream switch that trunks Campus 1 VLANs toward mswitch0
-- must be dropping PC5's VLAN on its trunk. Please confirm the switch4 trunk
fault and identify which VLAN it is dropping.

injection.action: move PC5's access port (eth2) from br_vlan10 to br_vlan1
injection.command:
ip link set eth2 nomaster
  ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1 2>/dev/null || (ip link add br_vlan1 type bridge; ip link set br_vlan1 up; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan1)

post_inject_check.command: bridge link show | grep eth2 | grep -c br_vlan10

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-switch1-pc5-wrong-vlan: switch1's eth2 (the
access port for PC5) was moved out of br_vlan10 into br_vlan1, the unused default
VLAN. PC5 still sends untagged frames expecting VLAN 10 semantics, but switch1 now
bridges them into VLAN 1 -- an L2 broadcast domain with no router attached -- so
ARP for the gateway gets no reply. Other hosts on br_vlan10 (PC6/PC7/PC8) are
unaffected.

The TWIST: the ticket blames switch4's trunk. switch4 is HEALTHY -- its trunk is
carrying VLAN 10 normally, which is exactly why PC6/PC7/PC8 (also in VLAN 10, on
the same path through switch4) still reach 172.16.10.254. If switch4 were dropping
VLAN 10, ALL of those PCs would fail, not just PC5. The single-host blast radius
is the decisive tell: a trunk dropping a VLAN is a shared failure; only a
per-port (access-port) change can break exactly one host while its VLAN peers stay
up.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = switch1 (eth2 VLAN
membership). The agent must localise from evidence -- only PC5 affected, its access
port is in the wrong VLAN on switch1 -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on
switch4's trunk. An agent that "confirms the switch4 trunk fault" has followed the
accusation instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on
switch1.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10` on switch1
scoring_axes: must-identify-access-port-wrong-vlan: PC5's access port (eth2) is in the wrong VLAN (VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10) on switch1

bonus-clears-switch4-trunk: exonerates switch4 by any valid evidence -- e.g. explicitly clearing its trunk, or demonstrating the fault is local to switch1/PC5 while other VLAN-10 hosts (PC6/PC7/PC8) work through the same trunk

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the VLAN membership on access port eth2 of switch1 (the Campus 1 access switch for VLAN10). PC5 (172.16.10.5) has link and a correct default route but cannot ARP or reach its gateway 172.16.10.254 or peers on 172.16.10.0/24. From PC6, pings to PC5 return “Destination Host Unreachable,” indicating L2 isolation.

On switch1, the bridge configuration shows eth2 is incorrectly in br_vlan1 (default VLAN) instead of br_vlan10:
- brctl show: br_vlan1 includes eth0, eth1, eth2; br_vlan10 includes eth0.10, eth1.10, eth3, eth4, eth5.
- The FDB confirms PC5’s MAC (f6:9f:94:01:33:a3) learned on br_vlan1 via eth2, while VLAN10 peers (PC6–PC8) are on br_vlan10.
- PC6 can ping the gateway and has ARP entry 00:01:97:e4:04:01 for 172.16.10.254, proving VLAN10 is correctly carried on the upstream trunks (eth0.10/eth1.10) and not dropped.

Localization: switch1, interface eth2 (the access port for PC5). Mechanism: PC5 is placed in VLAN1, so its broadcasts/ARP never reach the VLAN10 gateway or hosts; conversely, VLAN10 traffic never reaches PC5. Root cause: mis-assignment of switch1 eth2 to VLAN1 instead of VLAN10.

Corrective fix: remove eth2 from br_vlan1 and add it to br_vlan10 (make eth2 an access port in VLAN10). Example: ip link set eth2 nomaster; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10. After reassignment, PC5 should regain connectivity to 172.16.10.254 and VLAN10 peers. No trunk fault on switch4; no VLAN is being dropped there.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-access-port-wrong-vlan: PC5's access port (eth2) is in the wrong VLAN (VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10) on switch1
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies switch1's access port eth2 as placed in VLAN 1 (br_vlan1) instead of VLAN 10 (br_vlan10).

per_axis.axis: bonus-clears-switch4-trunk: exonerates switch4 by any valid evidence -- e.g. explicitly clearing its trunk, or demonstrating the fault is local to switch1/PC5 while other VLAN-10 hosts (PC6/PC7/PC8) work through the same trunk
per_axis.rationale: Agent demonstrates switch4's trunk carries VLAN10 (PC6 can reach the gateway and has the gateway ARP via eth0.10/eth1.10) and explicitly localizes the fault to switch1 eth2, exonerating switch4.
Reassigning eth2 from br_vlan1 to br_vlan10 (e.g., ip link set eth2 nomaster; ip link set eth2 master br_vlan10) exactly matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log contains the key observations (PC5 unreachable to gateway, PC5 has correct IP, switch1 shows eth2 in br_vlan1 while br_vlan10 contains the other VLAN10 ports, and PC6 can reach the gateway), and the writeup draws the correct L2-localization and fix. Evidence in the log supports the asserted VLAN misassignment and rules out a switch4 trunk fault.
